<h1 id="keycloak-admin-rest-api">Keycloak Admin REST API v1.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

This is a REST API reference for the Keycloak Admin REST API.

<h1 id="keycloak-admin-rest-api-attack-detection">Attack Detection</h1>

## Clear any user login failures for all users This can release temporary disabled users

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/attack-detection/brute-force/users \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/attack-detection/brute-force/users`

<h3 id="clear-any-user-login-failures-for-all-users-this-can-release-temporary-disabled-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|

<h3 id="clear-any-user-login-failures-for-all-users-this-can-release-temporary-disabled-users-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Add new authentication execution

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/authentication/executions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "authenticatorConfig": "string",
    "authenticator": "string",
    "authenticatorFlow": true,
    "requirement": "string",
    "priority": 0,
    "autheticatorFlow": true,
    "id": "string",
    "flowId": "string",
    "parentFlow": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /admin/realms/{realm}/authentication/executions`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "authenticatorConfig": "string",
  "authenticator": "string",
  "authenticatorFlow": true,
  "requirement": "string",
  "priority": 0,
  "autheticatorFlow": true,
  "id": "string",
  "flowId": "string",
  "parentFlow": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-new-authentication-execution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|
|body|body|[AuthenticationExecutionRepresentation](#schemaauthenticationexecutionrepresentation)|false|none|
|» authenticatorConfig|body|string|false|none|
|» authenticator|body|string|false|none|
|» authenticatorFlow|body|boolean|false|none|
|» requirement|body|string|false|none|
|» priority|body|integer(int32)|false|none|
|» autheticatorFlow|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.**|
|» id|body|string|false|none|
|» flowId|body|string|false|none|
|» parentFlow|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="add-new-authentication-execution-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="keycloak-admin-rest-api-clients">Clients</h1>

## Get clients belonging to the realm.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/clients \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients`

If a client can’t be retrieved from the storage due to a problem with the underlying storage, it is silently removed from the returned list. This ensures that concurrent modifications to the list don’t prevent callers from retrieving this list.

<h3 id="get-clients-belonging-to-the-realm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clientId|query|string|false|filter by clientId|
|first|query|integer(int32)|false|the first result|
|max|query|integer(int32)|false|the max results to return|
|q|query|string|false|none|
|search|query|boolean|false|whether this is a search query or a getClientById query|
|viewableOnly|query|boolean|false|filter clients that cannot be viewed in full by admin|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "string",
    "clientId": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "rootUrl": "string",
    "adminUrl": "string",
    "baseUrl": "string",
    "surrogateAuthRequired": true,
    "enabled": true,
    "alwaysDisplayInConsole": true,
    "clientAuthenticatorType": "string",
    "secret": "string",
    "registrationAccessToken": "string",
    "defaultRoles": [
      "string"
    ],
    "redirectUris": [
      "string"
    ],
```

## Get group hierarchy. Only `name` and `id` are returned. `subGroups` are only returned when using the `search` or `q` parameter. If none of these parameters is provided, the top-level groups are returned without `subGroups` being filled.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/groups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /admin/realms/{realm}/groups`

<h3 id="get-group-hierarchy-only-name-and-id-are-returned-subgroups-are-only-returned-when-using-the-search-or-q-parameter-if-none-of-these-parameters-is-provided-the-top-level-groups-are-returned-without-subgroups-being-filled-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|briefRepresentation|query|boolean|false|none|
|exact|query|boolean|false|none|
|first|query|integer(int32)|false|none|

<h1 id="keycloak-admin-rest-api-organizations">Organizations</h1>

## Returns a paginated list of organizations filtered according to the specified parameters

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/organizations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations`

<h3 id="returns-a-paginated-list-of-organizations-filtered-according-to-the-specified-parameters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|briefRepresentation|query|boolean|false|if false, return the full representation. Otherwise, only the basic fields are returned.|
|exact|query|boolean|false|Boolean which defines whether the param 'search' must match exactly or not|
|first|query|integer(int32)|false|The position of the first result to be processed (pagination offset)|
|identityProvider|query|string|false|The alias of an identity provider, to only return the organizations linked to it. Cannot be combined with 'q'|
|max|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of results to be returned - defaults to 10|
|q|query|string|false|A query to search for custom attributes, in the format 'key1:value2 key2:value2'|
|search|query|string|false|A String representing either an organization name or domain|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|

## Returns the organizations counts.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/organizations/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/count`

<h3 id="returns-the-organizations-counts-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|exact|query|boolean|false|Boolean which defines whether the param 'search' must match exactly or not|
|identityProvider|query|string|false|The alias of an identity provider, to only count the organizations linked to it. Cannot be combined with 'q'|
|q|query|string|false|A query to search for custom attributes, in the format 'key1:value2 key2:value2'|
|search|query|string|false|A String representing either an organization name or domain|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
0
```

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|

<aside class="success">

</aside>

```json
}
```

## Returns a paginated list of organization members filtered according to the specified parameters

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/organizations/string/members \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/{org-id}/members`

<h3 id="returns-a-paginated-list-of-organization-members-filtered-according-to-the-specified-parameters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|briefRepresentation|query|boolean|false|Boolean to return either a brief or a full user representation. If not specified, the brief representation is returned by default.|
|exact|query|boolean|false|Boolean which defines whether the param 'search' must match exactly or not|
|first|query|integer(int32)|false|The position of the first result to be processed (pagination offset)|
|max|query|integer(int32)|false|The maximum number of results to be returned. Defaults to 10|
|membershipType|query|string|false|The membership type|
|search|query|string|false|A String representing either a member's username, e-mail, first name, or last name.|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|
|org-id|path|string|true|none|

## Adds the user with the specified id as a member of the organization

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/organizations/string/members \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '"string"'
```

`POST /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/{org-id}/members`

Adds, or associates, an existing user with the organization. If no user is found, or if it is already associated with the organization, an error response is returned

> Body parameter

```json
"string"
```

<h3 id="adds-the-user-with-the-specified-id-as-a-member-of-the-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|
|org-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|string|true|Payload should contain only id of the user to be added to the organization (UUID with or without quotes). Surrounding whitespace characters will be trimmed.|

<h3 id="adds-the-user-with-the-specified-id-as-a-member-of-the-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Invites an existing user or sends a registration link to a new user, based on the provided e-mail address.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/organizations/string/members/invite-user \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'email=string&firstName=string&lastName=string'
```

`POST /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/{org-id}/members/invite-user`

If the user with the given e-mail address exists, it sends an invitation link, otherwise it sends a registration link. The client_id query parameter is optional. If no client_id is provided, the account client is used. After accepting the invitation the user is redirected to the selected client's home URL; for the account client the organization redirect URL is used instead when configured.

> Body parameter

```yaml
email: string
firstName: string
lastName: string
```

<h3 id="invites-an-existing-user-or-sends-a-registration-link-to-a-new-user-based-on-the-provided-e-mail-address-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|query|string|false|Client id|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|
|org-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» email|body|string|false|none|
|» firstName|body|string|false|none|
|» lastName|body|string|false|none|

<h3 id="invites-an-existing-user-or-sends-a-registration-link-to-a-new-user-based-on-the-provided-e-mail-address-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Removes the user with the specified id from the organization

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/organizations/string/members/string \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/organizations/{org-id}/members/{member-id}`

Breaks the association between the user and organization. The user itself is deleted in case the membership is managed, otherwise the user is not deleted. If no user is found, or if they are not a member of the organization, an error response is returned

<h3 id="removes-the-user-with-the-specified-id-from-the-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|member-id|path|string|true|none|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|
|org-id|path|string|true|none|

<h3 id="removes-the-user-with-the-specified-id-from-the-organization-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h3 id="get-accessible-realms-returns-a-list-of-accessible-realms-the-list-is-filtered-based-on-what-realms-the-caller-is-allowed-to-view-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|

<h3 id="get-accessible-realms-returns-a-list-of-accessible-realms-the-list-is-filtered-based-on-what-realms-the-caller-is-allowed-to-view-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[RealmRepresentation](#schemarealmrepresentation)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Import a realm. Imports a realm from a full representation of that realm.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '"string"'
```

`POST /admin/realms`

Realm name must be unique.

<h3 id="import-a-realm-imports-a-realm-from-a-full-representation-of-that-realm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|string(binary)|false|none|

<h3 id="import-a-realm-imports-a-realm-from-a-full-representation-of-that-realm-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Created|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|None|
|500|Internal Server Error|Internal Server Error|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get the top-level representation of the realm It will not include nested information like User and Client representations.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /admin/realms/{realm}`

<h3 id="get-the-top-level-representation-of-the-realm-it-will-not-include-nested-information-like-user-and-client-representations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|

<h3 id="get-the-top-level-representation-of-the-realm-it-will-not-include-nested-information-like-user-and-client-representations-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[RealmRepresentation](#schemarealmrepresentation)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

|---|---|---|---|---|

|» defaultSignatureAlgorithm|body|string|false|none|
|» revokeRefreshToken|body|boolean|false|none|

## Partial import from a JSON file to an existing realm.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/partialImport \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '"string"'
```

`POST /admin/realms/{realm}/partialImport`

<h3 id="partial-import-from-a-json-file-to-an-existing-realm-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|
|body|body|string(binary)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

<h3 id="partial-import-from-a-json-file-to-an-existing-realm-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Remove a specific user session.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/sessions/string \
  -X DELETE
```

`DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/sessions/{session}`

Any client that has an admin url will also be told to invalidate this particular session.

<h3 id="remove-a-specific-user-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|session|path|string|true|none|
|isOffline|query|boolean|false|none|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|

<h3 id="remove-a-specific-user-session-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="keycloak-admin-rest-api-users">Users</h1>

## Get users Returns a stream of users, filtered according to query parameters.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users`

Returns a stream of users. Note that the 'credentials' field in the returned UserRepresentation objects is typically not populated for performance reasons. If specific credential metadata is required, use the dedicated 'GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user-id}/credentials' endpoint.

<h3 id="get-users-returns-a-stream-of-users-filtered-according-to-query-parameters-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|briefRepresentation|query|boolean|false|Boolean which defines whether brief representations are returned (default: false)|
|createdAfter|query|string|false|Only return users created after (inclusive) the given date, in ISO-8601 format (yyyy-MM-dd) or epoch milliseconds|
|createdBefore|query|string|false|Only return users created before (inclusive) the given date, in ISO-8601 format (yyyy-MM-dd) or epoch milliseconds|
|email|query|string|false|A String contained in email, or the complete email, if param "exact" is true|
|emailVerified|query|boolean|false|whether the email has been verified|
|enabled|query|boolean|false|Boolean representing if user is enabled or not|
|exact|query|boolean|false|Boolean which defines whether the params "last", "first", "email" and "username" must match exactly|
|first|query|integer(int32)|false|Pagination offset|
|firstName|query|string|false|A String contained in firstName, or the complete firstName, if param "exact" is true|
|idpAlias|query|string|false|The alias of an Identity Provider linked to the user|
|idpUserId|query|string|false|The userId at an Identity Provider linked to the user|
|lastName|query|string|false|A String contained in lastName, or the complete lastName, if param "exact" is true|
|max|query|integer(int32)|false|Maximum results size (defaults to 100)|
|q|query|string|false|A query to search for custom attributes, in the format 'key1:value2 key2:value2'|
|search|query|string|false|A String contained in username, first or last name, or email. Default search behavior is prefix-based (e.g., foo or foo*). Use *foo* for infix search and "foo" for exact search.|
|username|query|string|false|A String contained in username, or the complete username, if param "exact" is true|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|

## Returns the number of users that match the given criteria.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/users/count \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /admin/realms/{realm}/users/count`

It can be called in three different ways. 1. Don’t specify any criteria and pass {@code null}. The number of all users within that realm will be returned. <p> 2. If {@code search} is specified other criteria such as {@code last} will be ignored even though you set them. The {@code search} string will be matched against the first and last name, the username and the email of a user. <p> 3. If {@code search} is unspecified but any of {@code last}, {@code first}, {@code email} or {@code username} those criteria are matched against their respective fields on a user entity. Combined with a logical and.

<h3 id="returns-the-number-of-users-that-match-the-given-criteria-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|createdAfter|query|string|false|Only return users created after (inclusive) the given date, in ISO-8601 format (yyyy-MM-dd) or epoch milliseconds|
|createdBefore|query|string|false|Only return users created before (inclusive) the given date, in ISO-8601 format (yyyy-MM-dd) or epoch milliseconds|
|email|query|string|false|A String contained in email, or the complete email, if param "exact" is true|
|emailVerified|query|boolean|false|whether the email has been verified|
|enabled|query|boolean|false|Boolean representing if user is enabled or not|
|exact|query|boolean|false|Boolean which defines whether the params "last", "first", "email" and "username" must match exactly|
|firstName|query|string|false|A String contained in firstName, or the complete firstName, if param "exact" is true|
|idpAlias|query|string|false|The alias of an Identity Provider linked to the user|
|idpUserId|query|string|false|The userId at an Identity Provider linked to the user|
|lastName|query|string|false|A String contained in lastName, or the complete lastName, if param "exact" is true|
|q|query|string|false|A query to search for custom attributes, in the format 'key1:value2 key2:value2'|
|search|query|string|false|A String contained in username, first or last name, or email. Default search behavior is prefix-based (e.g., foo or foo*). Use *foo* for infix search and "foo" for exact search.|
|username|query|string|false|A String contained in username, or the complete username, if param "exact" is true|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
0
```

<h3 id="returns-the-number-of-users-that-match-the-given-criteria-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Send an email to the user with a link they can click to execute particular actions.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://keycloak.example.com/admin/realms/string/users/string/execute-actions-email \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '[
    "string"
  ]'
```

`PUT /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user-id}/execute-actions-email`

An email contains a link the user can click to perform a set of required actions. The redirectUri and clientId parameters are optional. If no redirect is given, then there will be no link back to click after actions have completed. Redirect uri must be a valid uri for the particular clientId.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  "string"
]
```

<h3 id="send-an-email-to-the-user-with-a-link-they-can-click-to-execute-particular-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|client_id|query|string|false|Client id|
|lifespan|query|integer(int32)|false|Number of seconds after which the generated token expires|
|redirect_uri|query|string|false|Redirect uri|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|
|user-id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[string]|false|none|

```bash
  -X POST
```

Activate the workflow for the given resource type and identifier. Optionally schedule the first step using the notBefore parameter.

|type|path|object|true|Resource type|
|notBefore|query|string|false|Optional value representing the time to schedule the first workflow step. The value is either an integer representing the seconds from now, an integer followed by 'ms' representing milliseconds from now, or an ISO-8601 date string.|
|realm|path|string|true|realm name (not id!)|
|id|path|string|true|Workflow identifier|

|---|---|---|---|

|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
